title: Add production readiness quickstart aligned with Console onboarding checklist
author: Wei Chen
description: This adds a new end-to-end “Production Readiness” quickstart intended to mirror the Console onboarding / first production launch checklist. The quickstart walks a new Hosted API user from: API key setup → first request → streaming → retries/timeouts → usage visibility → quotas/budgets guardrails → basic observability hooks → model pinning + fallback (conceptual; uses config placeholders). Motivation: we keep seeing early prod launches fail on 401/403 setup mistakes, streaming disconnect confusion, and 429 surprises; the checklist in Console helps, but we need a canonical runnable path customers can copy/paste and deploy. Scope: adds a new quickstart directory with Python + TypeScript examples (Go is stubbed with TODO and links to the SDK guide), adds a minimal “healthcheck” endpoint pattern, structured logs, and a tiny dashboard note for usage-lag expectations. Includes guidance for where to configure quotas/budgets in Console and links out to Terraform sample budget alerts. Non-goals: full guided tour, Dedicated/Private specifics, deep integration with the checklist progress service (this is docs/examples only).
commits: python: add prod-ready chat + streaming + retry presets
typescript: add streaming example + reconnect notes + structured logging
docs: link out to quotas/budgets + usage dashboard expectations
ci: add lightweight smoke tests for new quickstart
notable_snippets: Python (timeouts/retries): client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"], timeout_s=30, max_retries=3, backoff_initial_s=0.5, backoff_max_s=8.0)

TypeScript (streaming with reconnect note): for await (const event of client.chat.completions.stream({...})) { /* handle deltas */ } // if connection drops mid-stream, treat as non-idempotent and retry only when safe (see README)
Structured logging fields: request_id, model, route, status_code, latency_ms, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens
test_plan: 1) Local Python: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...; cd production-readiness/python; python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt; python app/main.py --non-streaming; python app/main.py --streaming. 2) Local TypeScript: cd production-readiness/typescript; npm ci; npm run start -- --non-streaming; npm run start -- --streaming. 3) Trigger 429 behavior: set low per-minute limit in Console (or use provided instructions to request temporary low quota), run load script in README, confirm exponential backoff and log output. 4) Observability: confirm logs include request_id + latency_ms; optionally set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and run sample docker-compose from observability.md. 5) CI smoke: workflow runs dependency install + one non-streaming request behind a secret-less stub (mocked transport) to ensure compilation + basic execution paths don’t regress.
docs_and_checklist_alignment: Checklist mapping is called out in production-readiness/README.md under “Checklist parity”. Steps covered: API key + env vars, first successful request, streaming, retries/timeouts, usage dashboard + expected lag, quotas/budgets basics, basic observability hooks, model pinning guidance + fallback policy concepts (links to docs; no server-side config changes here).
screenshots: N/A (README-driven quickstart). Sample output blocks included in README for both languages.
